data.text:
NOW: Thousands will pour into Luneta Park and the People Power Monument on EDSA from various points across Metro Manila this Bonifacio Day—with more demonstrations taking place across the country—as they again drum up the fight against the persistent crisis of government corruption.

“Baha sa Luneta 2.0,” led by the alliance Kilusang Bayan Kontra Korakot and multisectoral groups, will begin its main program at 9 a.m. They will attempt a march to the foot of Mendiola later in the afternoon. At the same time, the “Trillion Peso March”—composed mainly of the Tindig Pilipinas coalition, as well as religious and civil society organizations—will take place along EDSA with a program extending into the early evening.

Sunday’s massive, wide-ranging protests follow the last set of events that took place on Sept. 21, which coincided with the 53rd anniversary of Martial Law. Similarly, Nov. 30—a holiday commemorating the birth of the revolutionary and Katipunan leader—will be marked by demands ranging from calls for transparency to the resignation of the nation’s top leaders altogether.

BAHA SA LUNETA 2.0 HINAHARANG? 

Hindi makapag-asembol ang organizers ng Baha sa Luneta 2.0 ng entablado sa kahabaang ito ng Roxas Blvd. 

Ayon kay BAYAN Secretary General Mong Palatino, hinarang sila ng pulisyang naghahanap ng permit. 

Alas-12 ng hatinggabi pa aniya dapat naka-setup ang stage at ipinatupad ang road closure para rito. 

Idiniin ng Sec-Gen na koordinado naman ang rally sa Manila LGU at MMDA na nagbigay ng pagsigurong ibibigay ang assistance kagaya sa INC rally kamakailan. 

“We believe the ongoing attempt to derail the Luneta protest is linked to the overkill, unnecessary, disproportionate, and paranoid security preparations around the vicinity of Recto, Mendiola, and Malacanang,” dagdag pa niya. | RH 15 @JecelleRicafort, DZRH News

Manila Police District Spokesperson Philipp Ines tells Inquirer that they did not receive instructions from the Manila City government to allow the Baha sa Luneta 2.0 anti-corruption rally without a permit.

“Wala tayong nakukuhang impormasyon galing sa LGU at kung meron man, meron dapat silang hawak na permit,” Ines said.
